claim: Antiretroviral therapy for HIV-1 infection/AIDS has significantly extended the life expectancy of HIV-1-infected individuals.
source: Antiretroviral therapy for HIV-1 infection/AIDS has significantly extended the life expectancy of HIV-1-infected individuals and reduced HIV-1 transmission at very high rates.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Samji et al., 2013; Marcus et al., 2016) as stated in the Introduction section.

claim: Antiretroviral therapy has reduced HIV-1 transmission at very high rates.
source: Antiretroviral therapy for HIV-1 infection/AIDS has significantly extended the life expectancy of HIV-1-infected individuals and reduced HIV-1 transmission at very high rates.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature as stated in the Introduction section.

claim: GRL-142 is a novel HIV-1 protease inhibitor containing an unprecedented 6-5-5-ring-fused crown-like tetrahydropyranofuran.
source: Here, we report GRL-142, a novel HIV-1 protease inhibitor containing an unprecedented 6-5-5-ring-fused crown-like tetrahydropyranofuran, which has extremely potent activity against all HIV-1 strains examined with IC50 values of attomolar-to-picomolar concentrations
evidence: The structure of GRL-142 is described in the text and shown in Figure 1.

claim: GRL-142 has extremely potent activity against all HIV-1 strains examined with IC50 values of attomolar-to-picomolar concentrations.
source: Here, we report GRL-142, a novel HIV-1 protease inhibitor containing an unprecedented 6-5-5-ring-fused crown-like tetrahydropyranofuran, which has extremely potent activity against all HIV-1 strains examined with IC50 values of attomolar-to-picomolar concentrations
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Tables 1-4 showing IC50 values in the attomolar to picomolar range.

claim: GRL-142 has virtually no effects on cellular growth.
source: which has extremely potent activity against all HIV-1 strains examined with IC50 values of attomolar-to-picomolar concentrations, virtually no effects on cellular growth
evidence: This is supported by the high CC50 value (47 μM) and selectivity index (2,473,684) shown in Table 2.

claim: GRL-142 has extremely high genetic barrier against the emergence of drug-resistant variants.
source: which has extremely potent activity against all HIV-1 strains examined with IC50 values of attomolar-to-picomolar concentrations, virtually no effects on cellular growth, extremely high genetic barrier against the emergence of drug-resistant variants
evidence: This is supported by the in vitro selection experiments shown in Figure 4A demonstrating that HIV-1 failed to develop resistance to GRL-142 over 36 weeks.

claim: GRL-142 has favorable intracellular penetration.
source: which has extremely potent activity against all HIV-1 strains examined with IC50 values of attomolar-to-picomolar concentrations, virtually no effects on cellular growth, extremely high genetic barrier against the emergence of drug-resistant variants, and favorable intracellular and central nervous system penetration.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2E showing significantly higher intracellular concentrations of GRL-142 compared to DRV in PBMCs.

claim: GRL-142 has favorable central nervous system penetration.
source: which has extremely potent activity against all HIV-1 strains examined with IC50 values of attomolar-to-picomolar concentrations, virtually no effects on cellular growth, extremely high genetic barrier against the emergence of drug-resistant variants, and favorable intracellular and central nervous system penetration.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4B showing GRL-142 concentrations in rat brain that are ~1,882 fold greater than its IC50 value.

claim: GRL-142 forms optimum polar, van der Waals, and halogen bond interactions with HIV-1 protease.
source: GRL-142 forms optimum polar, van der Waals, and halogen bond interactions with HIV-1 protease and strongly blocks protease dimerization
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3 and Table 5.

claim: GRL-142 strongly blocks protease dimerization.
source: GRL-142 forms optimum polar, van der Waals, and halogen bond interactions with HIV-1 protease and strongly blocks protease dimerization
evidence: This is supported by FRET-based assay data shown in Figure 2B and ESI-MS data in Figure 2C.

claim: Mortality rates for HIV-1-infected individuals who are treated before they have substantial immunologic damage have become close to that of general population.
source: Indeed, mortality rates for HIV-1-infected individuals who are treated before they have substantial immunologic damage have become close to that of general population and cART has been shown to reduce sexual transmission of HIV-1 by 93–96% (Cohen et al., 2011; Cohen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies (Cohen et al., 2011; Cohen et al., 2016).

claim: cART has been shown to reduce sexual transmission of HIV-1 by 93–96%.
source: Indeed, mortality rates for HIV-1-infected individuals who are treated before they have substantial immunologic damage have become close to that of general population and cART has been shown to reduce sexual transmission of HIV-1 by 93–96% (Cohen et al., 2011; Cohen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies (Cohen et al., 2011; Cohen et al., 2016).

claim: At the end of 2015, ~36.7 million people were living with HIV-1 infection.
source: Yet, at the end of 2015, ~36.7 million people were living with HIV-1 infection, and 2.1 million people were newly infected and 1.7 million people lost their lives only in 2015 (http://www.unaids.org/sites/default/files/media_asset/global-AIDS-update-2016_en.pdf).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a UNAIDS report.

claim: In 2015, 2.1 million people were newly infected with HIV-1.
source: Yet, at the end of 2015, ~36.7 million people were living with HIV-1 infection, and 2.1 million people were newly infected and 1.7 million people lost their lives only in 2015 (http://www.unaids.org/sites/default/files/media_asset/global-AIDS-update-2016_en.pdf).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a UNAIDS report.

claim: In 2015, 1.7 million people lost their lives to HIV-1/AIDS.
source: Yet, at the end of 2015, ~36.7 million people were living with HIV-1 infection, and 2.1 million people were newly infected and 1.7 million people lost their lives only in 2015 (http://www.unaids.org/sites/default/files/media_asset/global-AIDS-update-2016_en.pdf).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a UNAIDS report.

claim: The cure of HIV-1 infection or AIDS is still elusive.
source: However, the cure of HIV-1 infection or AIDS is still elusive (Deeks et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Deeks et al., 2016).

claim: Protease inhibitors generally have high genetic barrier against resistance.
source: Nevertheless, in regard to the propensity of HIV-1 to develop resistance to antiretroviral agents, protease inhibitors (PIs) generally have high genetic barrier against resistance.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about HIV-1 protease inhibitors.

claim: Darunavir is the only PI recommended for first line therapy.
source: In particular, the latest U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved PI, darunavir (DRV), the only PI recommended for first line therapy (Panel on Antiretroviral Guidelines for Adults and Adolescents, 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to treatment guidelines (Panel on Antiretroviral Guidelines for Adults and Adolescents, 2016).

claim: Darunavir has a favorable genetic barrier apparently because of its dual mechanism of action: (i) protease enzymatic inhibition activity and (ii) protease dimerization inhibition activity.
source: has a favorable genetic barrier apparently because of its dual mechanism of action: (i) protease enzymatic inhibition activity and (ii) protease dimerization inhibition activity (Koh et al., 2007; Koh et al., 2011; Hayashi et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies (Koh et al., 2007; Koh et al., 2011; Hayashi et al., 2014).

claim: Darunavir currently represents the most widely used PI for treating HIV-1-infected individuals.
source: and currently represents the most widely used PI for treating HIV-1-infected individuals.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about current HIV treatment practices.

claim: The emergence of DRV-resistant HIV-1 variants has been reported both in vitro and in vivo.
source: Nevertheless, the emergence of DRV-resistant HIV-1 variants has been reported both in vitro and in vivo, and patients with such DRV-resistant HIV-1 variants may experience treatment failure (Koh et al., 2010; Mitsuya et al., 2007; De Meyer et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies (Koh et al., 2010; Mitsuya et al., 2007; De Meyer et al., 2009).

claim: 12–21% of individuals receiving DRV-containing regimens discontinue the treatment due to adverse events, mainly diarrhea and virological failure.
source: Furthermore, 12–21% of individuals receiving DRV-containing regimens discontinue the treatment due to adverse events, mainly diarrhea and virological failure (Clotet et al., 2007; Madruga et al., 2007; Ortiz et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published clinical studies (Clotet et al., 2007; Madruga et al., 2007; Ortiz et al., 2008).

claim: Atazanavir frequently causes indirect hyperbilirubinemia.
source: An alternative PI, atazanavir (ATV), also frequently causes indirect hyperbilirubinemia(Lennox et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Lennox et al., 2014).

claim: Serious adverse events such as gastrointestinal disorders have been seen in as high as 11% of individuals receiving DTG.
source: However, serious adverse events such as gastrointestinal disorders have been seen in as high as 11% of individuals receiving DTG (Clotet et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Clotet et al., 2014).

claim: HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders (HAND) occur in 40–83% HIV-1-infected individuals.
source: In addition, cART has less benefit in patients with progressive neuropsychological impairment such as HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders (HAND), which occur in 40–83% HIV-1-infected individuals (Heaton et al., 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature (Heaton et al., 2010).

claim: Patients with HAND are less likely to achieve long-term virologic suppression.
source: and these patients are less likely to achieve long-term virologic suppression (Tozzi et al., 2005; Saylor et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies (Tozzi et al., 2005; Saylor et al., 2016).

claim: GRL-142 contains newly generated pharmacophores such as an unprecedented 6-5-5 ring-fused crown-like tetrahydropyranofuran (Crn-THF) as the P2-ligand, P1-bis-fluoro-benzyl (bis-Fbz), and P2′-cyclopropyl-amino-benzothiazole (Cp-Abt).
source: GRL-142 contains newly generated pharmacophores such as an unprecedented 6-5-5 ring-fused crown-like tetrahydropyranofuran (Crn-THF) as the P2-ligand, P1-bis-fluoro-benzyl (bis-Fbz), and P2′-cyclopropyl-amino-benzothiazole (Cp-Abt)(Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by the chemical structure shown in Figure 1.

claim: GRL-139 exerts comparable antiviral activity against wild-type HIV-1 (cHIVNL4-3WT) as compared to DRV.
source: GRL-139, a prototype to GRL-142, structurally resembles DRV but contains the Crn-THF moiety instead of the bis-THF of DRV (Figure 1), and exerts comparable antiviral activity against wild-type HIV-1 (cHIVNL4-3WT) as compared to DRV (Table 1) (Ghosh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by IC50 data in Table 1 and citation to published work (Ghosh et al., 2017).

claim: GRL-139 failed to block the replication of three highly DRV-resistant HIV-1 variants (HIVDRVRs).
source: However, GRL-139 failed to block the replication of three highly DRV-resistant HIV-1 variants (HIVDRVRs) that were selected by propagating in the presence of increasing concentrations of DRV and are highly resistant to all presently clinically available PIs including DRV and nucleos(t)ide-reverse-transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) such as tenofovir (TDF) (Koh et al., 2010; Aoki et al., 2015) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Table 1 showing high IC50 values for GRL-139 against HIVDRVRs.

claim: GRL-036 more effectively blocks the replication of HIVDRVRs than DRV.
source: By contrast, GRL-036 also resembles DRV but has the Cp-Abt moiety and shows an improved anti-HIV-1 profile, more effectively blocking the replication of HIVDRVRs than DRV (Table 1) (Ghosh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by IC50 data in Table 1 and citation to published work (Ghosh et al., 2017).

claim: GRL-121 more effectively blocked the replication of cHIVNL4-3WT by about 10-fold compared to DRV.
source: GRL-121 contains both Crn-THF and Cp-Abt moieties and more effectively blocked the replication of cHIVNL4-3WT by about 10-fold compared to DRV (Ghosh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by IC50 data in Table 1 showing GRL-121 IC50 of 0.26 nM vs DRV IC50 of 3.2 nM, and citation to published work (Ghosh et al., 2017).

claim: GRL-121 more potently suppressed the replication of all three HIVDRVRs.
source: GRL-121 more potently suppressed the replication of all three HIVDRVRs.
evidence: This is supported by IC50 data in Table 1.

claim: The addition of two fluorine atoms to GRL-121, generating GRL-142 further strengthened the activity against cHIVNL4-3WT achieving an IC50 value as low as 0.019 nM.
source: Interestingly, the addition of two fluorine atoms to GRL-121, generating GRL-142 further strengthened the activity against cHIVNL4-3WT achieving an IC50 value as low as 0.019 nM compared to the 9 FDA-approved PIs of which IC50s range from 3.2 to 330 nM (Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by IC50 data in Tables 1 and 2.

claim: GRL-142 had a much improved cytotoxicity profile with a selectivity index (CC50/IC50) as high as 2,473,684.
source: GRL-142 had a much improved cytotoxicity profile with a selectivity index (CC50/IC50) as high as 2,473,684 (Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by cytotoxicity data in Table 2.

claim: GRL-142 highly potently blocked the replication of all three HIVDRVRs by factors of 27–83 compared to GRL-121.
source: GRL-142 also highly potently blocked the replication of all three HIVDRVRs by factors of 27–83 compared to GRL-121 (Table 1)
evidence: This is supported by IC50 data in Table 1.

claim: The most DRV-resistant HIV-1 variant, HIVDRVRP51, is less sensitive to GRL-142 by 63-fold than cHIVNL4-3WT.
source: while it should be noted that the most DRV-resistant HIV-1 variant, HIVDRVRP51, is less sensitive to GRL-142 by 63-fold than cHIVNL4-3WT, indicating considerable resistance shift.
evidence: This is supported by IC50 data in Table 1 showing fold-change of 63.

claim: The IC50 value of GRL-142 against HIVDRVRP51 (1.2 nM) was ~3 fold lower than that of DRV against cHIVNL4-3WT (3.2 nM).
source: Notably, the IC50 value of GRL-142 against HIVDRVRP51 (1.2 nM), the most multi-PI/NRTI-resistant HIVDRVR, was ~3 fold lower than that of DRV against cHIVNL4-3WT (3.2 nM).
evidence: This is supported by IC50 data in Table 1.

claim: GRL-142 exerts highly potent antiviral activity against the HIV-2 strains examined.
source: We further examined the activity of GRL-142 against two HIV-2 strains and found that GRL-142 also exerts highly potent antiviral activity against the HIV-2 strains examined (Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by IC50 data in Table 2 showing IC50 values of 0.00032 nM and 0.000059 nM for HIV-2ROD and HIV-2EHO, respectively.

claim: DRV has been shown to effectively disrupt the dimerization of PR monomer subunits as determined by the fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based HIV-1 expression assay.
source: In this regard, DRV has been shown to effectively disrupt the dimerization of PR monomer subunits as determined by the fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based HIV-1 expression assay (Koh et al., 2007) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published work (Koh et al., 2007) and data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In the absence of compounds, the mean CFPA/B ratio obtained was 1.16, indicating that PR dimerization clearly occurred.
source: In the absence of compounds, the mean CFPA/B ratio obtained was 1.16, indicating that PR dimerization clearly occurred (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by FRET assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The CFPA/B ratio was decreased to 0.91 in the presence of 100 nM DRV, demonstrating that DRV blocked the dimerization of the PR subunit.
source: However, the ratio was decreased to 0.91 in the presence of 100 nM DRV, demonstrating that DRV blocked the dimerization of the PR subunit.
evidence: This is supported by FRET assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: GRL-142 blocked the dimerization at much lower concentrations (0.1 nM) than DRV.
source: Interestingly, GRL-142 blocked the dimerization at much lower concentrations (0.1 nM) than DRV.
evidence: This is supported by FRET assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: GRL-142 has bimodal HIV-1 inhibition mechanism, (i) inhibition of HIV-1 PR dimerization and (ii) inhibition of enzymatic activity of PR.
source: These data strongly suggest that as in the case of DRV, GRL-142 has bimodal HIV-1 inhibition mechanism, (i) inhibition of HIV-1 PR dimerization and (ii) inhibition of enzymatic activity of PR.
evidence: This is inferred from the FRET assay data in Figure 2B and established knowledge about protease inhibitor mechanisms.

claim: GRL-142 more tightly bound to monomers by 6.78-fold and to dimers by 3.13-fold than DRV.
source: When compared with the heights of the dimer+monomer peak rendered 1.0, the average height of the three peaks of DRV-bound monomers and that of the three peaks of GRL-142-bound monomers were 0.046 and 0.312, respectively; and the average height of the three peaks with DRV-bound dimers and that of the three peaks with GRL-142-bound dimers were 0.060 and 0.188, respectively. These data suggest that GRL-142 more tightly bound to monomers by 6.78-fold and to dimers by 3.13-fold than DRV
evidence: This is supported by ESI-MS data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The Tm value of PRD25N alone was 54.92˚C.
source: As illustrated in Figure 2D, the Tm value of PRD25N alone was 54.92˚C
evidence: This is supported by DSF data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In the presence of SQV, the Tm value of PRD25N increased to 58.14˚C.
source: while in the presence of SQV and DRV, the values increased to 58.14˚C and 58.21˚C, respectively
evidence: This is supported by DSF data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In the presence of DRV, the Tm value of PRD25N increased to 58.21˚C.
source: while in the presence of SQV and DRV, the values increased to 58.14˚C and 58.21˚C, respectively
evidence: This is supported by DSF data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In the presence of GRL-142, the Tm value of PRD25N was 65.65˚C.
source: However, in the presence of GRL-142, the Tm value of PRD25N turned out to be substantially high at 65.65˚C
evidence: This is supported by DSF data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The difference in Tm values between PRD25N alone and GRL-142-bound PRD25N reached as high as 10.73˚C.
source: and the difference in Tm values between PRD25N alone and GRL-142-bound PRD25N reached as high as 10.73˚C, suggesting that GRL-142 more strongly binds to PRD25N than SQV or DRV.
evidence: This is calculated from the DSF data shown in Figure 2D (65.65 - 54.92 = 10.73).

claim: Fluorination increases lipophilicity because the carbon-fluorine bond is more hydrophobic than the carbon-hydrogen bond.
source: It is known that fluorination increases lipophilicity because the carbon-fluorine bond is more hydrophobic than the carbon-hydrogen bond, often enhancing cell membrane penetration and oral bioavailability of the compounds containing carbon-fluorine bond (Böhm et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature (Böhm et al., 2004).

claim: Intracellular concentrations of GRL-142 were significantly higher than those of DRV.
source: As shown in Figure 2E, intracellular concentrations of GRL-142 were significantly higher than those of DRV as examined under the same conditions.
evidence: This is supported by LC/MS data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: GRL-142 binds in the active site of PRWT in two distinct conformations (related by 180˚ rotation) with relative occupancies of 0.53 and 0.47.
source: GRL-142 binds in the active site of PRWT in two distinct conformations (related by 180˚ rotation) with relative occupancies of 0.53 and 0.47.
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data.

claim: The Crn-THF moiety of GRL-142 has two oxygen atoms and they both form hydrogen bonding interactions with the backbone amides of D29 and D30.
source: The Crn-THF moiety has two oxygen atoms and they both form hydrogen bonding interactions with the backbone amides of D29 and D30 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The thiazole nitrogen of GRL-142 makes a hydrogen bond interaction with the backbone NH of D30ʹ.
source: The thiazole nitrogen makes a hydrogen bond interaction with the backbone NH of D30ʹ.
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The P2ʹ amino group of GRL-142 forms polar interactions with the sidechain carboxylate of D30ʹ.
source: The P2ʹ amino group forms polar interactions with the sidechain carboxylate of D30ʹ.
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The carbonyl and sulfonyl oxygens of GRL-142 have polar interactions with the PR flap residues I50 and I50ʹ through a bridging water molecule.
source: The carbonyl and sulfonyl oxygens have polar interactions with the PR flap residues I50 and I50ʹ through a bridging water molecule.
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The transition state mimic hydroxyl group of GRL-142 forms polar interactions with the catalytic aspartates D25 and D25ʹ.
source: The transition state mimic hydroxyl group forms polar interactions with the catalytic aspartates D25 and D25ʹ.
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: There is a hydrogen bond interaction from the amide nitrogen of the carbamate moiety of GRL-142 to the backbone carbonyl oxygen of G27.
source: There is another hydrogen bond interaction from the amide nitrogen of the carbamate moiety to the backbone carbonyl oxygen of G27.
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The Crn-THF moiety of GRL-142 has more favorable vdW contacts with PRWT residues compared to the bis-THF moiety of DRV.
source: The Crn-THF (Figure 3B-top right panel) has more favorable vdW contacts with PRWT residues compared to the bis-THF moiety of DRV (Figure 3B-top left panel).
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The Crn-THF moiety of GRL-142 mediates better contacts with D29, D30, V32, I47, and L76 residues compared to the bis-THF moiety of DRV.
source: While the Crn-THF moiety of GRL-142 mediates better contacts with D29, D30, V32, I47, and L76 residues compared to the bis-THF moiety of DRV
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The Cp-Abt moiety of GRL-142 forms better vdW contacts with the residues of D30' of PRWT.
source: the Cp-Abt moiety also forms better vdW contacts with the residues of D30' of PRWT (Figure 3B-bottom right panel).
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The vdW energy of interactions between DRV and protease is −57.8 kcal/mol.
source: The vdW energy of interactions between DRV and protease is −57.8 kcal/mol.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Table 5.

claim: GRL-142 has vdW interaction energy with protease of −67.5 kcal/mol.
source: GRL-142 has much better vdW interactions with protease as demonstrated by its lower interaction energy of −67.5 kcal/mol.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Table 5.

claim: The improved vdW interaction energy of ~10 kcal/mol may partly explain the much superior antiviral activity of GRL-142 compared to that of DRV.
source: The improved vdW interaction energy of ~10 kcal/mol may partly explain the much superior antiviral activity of GRL-142 compared to that of DRV.
evidence: This is inferred from the molecular dynamics simulation data in Table 5 and antiviral activity data in Tables 1-4.

claim: GRL-142 has better interactions with Asp29/Asp29ʹ and Asp30/Asp30ʹ by ~3 kcal/mol compared to DRV.
source: GRL-142 has better interactions with Asp29/Asp29ʹ and Asp30/Asp30ʹ by ~3 kcal/mol.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Table 5.

claim: GRL-142 has a better interaction energy of ~3 kcal/mol with Ile47/Ile47ʹ compared to DRV.
source: Compared to DRV, GRL-142 also has a better interaction energy of ~3 kcal/mol with Ile47/Ile47ʹ which are located in the flap region of protease.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Table 5.

claim: Fluorine substitution in GRL-142 causes very favorable halogen interactions within the S1-pocket of PRWT.
source: The crystal structure indicates that fluorine substitution causes very favorable halogen interactions within the S1-pocket of PRWT (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The two fluorine atoms of GRL-142 establish a halogen bond bridge within the S1-pocket by interacting with residues of both subunits of PRWT.
source: Overall, the two fluorine atoms establish a halogen bond bridge within the S1-pocket by interacting with residues of both subunits of PRWT.
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: GRL-142 has good vdW contacts with wild-type V32.
source: As shown in Figure 3D, GRL-142 has good vdW contacts with wild-type V32
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: vdW interactions of GRL-142 with mutated I32 are much better than with V32, especially the interactions with I32ʹ.
source: however, vdW interactions proved to be much better with mutated I32, especially the interactions of GRL-142 with I32ʹ.
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: I32 and I32ʹ have an improved vdW interaction energy (~1 kcal/mol) with GRL-142 compared to V32 and V32ʹ.
source: Our simulations showed that I32 and I32ʹ have an improved vdW interaction energy (~1 kcal/mol) with GRL-142 compared to V32 and V32ʹ.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: When selected in the presence of ATV, the virus became resistant to the drugs and started replicating in the presence of 5 μM by 36 weeks.
source: When selected in the presence of ATV, the virus became resistant to the drugs and started replicating in the presence of 5 μM by 36 weeks (Figure 4A-top left panel).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro selection data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The PR-encoding region of the virus obtained from the culture concluded at week 36 with ATV contained seven amino acid substitutions, which were thought to be associated with the acquisition of HIV-1 resistance against ATV.
source: The PR-encoding region of the virus obtained from the culture concluded at week 36 contained seven amino acid substitutions, which were thought to be associated with the acquisition of HIV-1 resistance against ATV (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The development of DRV-resistant HIV-1 variants was significantly delayed and concentrations above 0.1 µM DRV still inhibited replication at week-36.
source: The development of DRV-resistant HIV-1 variants was significantly delayed and concentrations above 0.1 µM DRV still inhibited replication at week-36.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro selection data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: cHIVNL4-3WT failed to propagate in the presence of >0.01 μM of GRL-121 even at week 36.
source: However, cHIVNL4-3WT failed to propagate in the presence of >0.01 μM of GRL-121 and >0.003 μM of GRL-142 even at week 36 (Figure 4A-top left panel)
evidence: This is supported by in vitro selection data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: cHIVNL4-3WT failed to propagate in the presence of >0.003 μM of GRL-142 even at week 36.
source: However, cHIVNL4-3WT failed to propagate in the presence of >0.01 μM of GRL-121 and >0.003 μM of GRL-142 even at week 36 (Figure 4A-top left panel)
evidence: This is supported by in vitro selection data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: HIV-1 failed to select any meaningful resistant substitutions to GRL-121 and GRL-142.
source: indicating that HIV-1 failed to select any meaningful resistant substitutions.
evidence: This is inferred from the in vitro selection data shown in Figure 4A and sequencing data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The only substitutions that occurred with GRL-142 selection were G16E and A71T.
source: The only substitutions that occurred were G16E and A71T (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: G16 and A71 residues are located outside the active site of HIV-1 protease.
source: Both these residues are located outside the active site of HIV-1 protease.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of HIV-1 protease structure.

claim: When HIV11MIX was employed as a starting HIV-1 population, the virus quickly became highly resistant to both ATV and DRV.
source: When we employed a mixture of 11 multiple-PI-resistant clinical HIV-1 isolates (HIV11MIX) as a starting HIV-1 population, the virus quickly became highly resistant to both ATV and DRV (Figure 4A-top right panel and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is supported by in vitro selection data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: HIV11MIX failed to propagate in the presence of >0.07 µM GRL-121.
source: However, in the presence of >0.07 µM GRL-121 or >0.017 µM GRL-142, HIV11MIX failed to propagate.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro selection data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: HIV11MIX failed to propagate in the presence of >0.017 µM GRL-142.
source: However, in the presence of >0.07 µM GRL-121 or >0.017 µM GRL-142, HIV11MIX failed to propagate.
